title: [Bug] Calling a macro in a pre- or post-hook
body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt-core?

- [X] I believe this is a new bug in dbt-core
- [X] I have searched the existing issues, and I could not find an existing issue for this bug

### Current Behavior

There's 3 ways to define a pre-hook for a model:

1. In `dbt_project.yml`
2. In a property file (`properties.yml`)
3. In a config block (`my_model.sql`)

Calling a macro in a pre-hook works for 1. and 3. but not 2:
```yaml
# properties.yml
version: 2
models:
  - name: my_model
    config:
      pre-hook: "{{ my_macro() }}"
```

produces a compilation error
```bash
Could not render {{ my_macro() }}: 'my_macro' is undefined
```

### Expected Behavior

The behavior should be consistent across 1. 2. 3. Ideally, calling a macro for a pre-hook should work in property files too.

### Steps To Reproduce

See Current Behavior

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Environment

```markdown
- OS:
- Python:
- dbt: 1.4.3
```


### Which database adapter are you using with dbt?

snowflake

### Additional Context

https://getdbt.slack.com/archives/C50NEBJGG/p1677527674055049

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
### Acceptance criteria
1. A new test is added that verifies macros within pre- and post-hooks are late-rendered when they are specified within a [model properties YAML](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/model-properties) configuration file. Use YAML similar to that described in the "Current Behavior" above.
1. This test fails prior to implementing the feature.
1. This test succeeds after implementing this feature for `pre-hook`, `post-hook`, `pre_hook`, and `post_hook`.
1. Ensure that late-rendering tests exist for `dbt_project.yml` and model config blocks also.

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
Multiple people have reported the desire to put _all_ configs within `properties.yml` YAML files (rather than having some configs within individual model files).

Resolving this issue will provide that capability. In the meantime, a workaround is provided below along with a reproducible example (reprex).

### Reprex

This works when running `dbt compile`, `dbt run`, `dbt build`, etc:

`models/my_model.sql`

```sql
{{ config(
    pre_hook="{{ some_macro() }}"
) }}

select 1 as id
```

And so does this:

`dbt_project.yml`

```yaml
name: my_project
profile: my_profile

models:
  my_project:
    +pre-hook: "{{ some_macro() }}"
```

But this doesn't:

`models/_properties.yml`

```yaml
models:
  - name: my_model
    config:
      pre_hook: "{{ some_macro() }}"
```

And it gives this error message:

```
14:31:46  Encountered an error:
Compilation Error
  Could not render {{ some_macro() }}: 'some_macro' is undefined
```

### Workaround

In the meantime, the workaround is to put hook configs within model files instead of `properties.yml` / `schema.yml`:

```sql
{{ config(
    pre_hook="{{ some_macro() }}"
) }}

...
```

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
@rbs392 See below for something you could try out for dbt python models. I didn't try it out personally, so let me know if it works or not 🙏

Let's suppose you have a python model at the path `models/subfolder_1/subfolder_2/my_python_model.sql`. Then you could try this within `dbt_project.yml`:

```yaml
name: my_project
profile: my_profile

models:
  my_project:
    subfolder_1:
      subfolder_2:
        my_python_model:
          +pre-hook: "{{ some_macro() }}"
```

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
I ran into this myself this week.

The solution would be [late-rendering](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/issues/2818) hooks that appear within [`properties.yml`](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/configs-and-properties#where-can-i-define-properties) files (like https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/pull/6435 added late-rendering for `pre_hook` and `post_hook` in `dbt_project.yml`).

The relevant code appears to be `should_render_keypath` / [`_is_norender_key`](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/c668846404c78ea7317dc0523b49703c61c9885f/core/dbt/parser/schema_renderer.py#L23) within the `SchemaYamlRenderer` class.

The analogous code for `dbt_project.yml` is [`should_render_keypath`](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/c668846404c78ea7317dc0523b49703c61c9885f/core/dbt/config/renderer.py#L170) within the `DbtProjectYamlRenderer` class.

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
To expand on the use-case of [adding a post hook to a seed in a properties YAML file](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/7128#issuecomment-2069110265), here's an example:

```yaml
seeds:
  - name: seed_name
    config:
      post_hook: "alter table {{ this }} alter column id set not null"
    columns:
      - name: id
```

But when running `dbt seed`, I got an error like this because `{{ this }}` wasn't late-rendered:
```
13:43:24    Database Error in seed seed_name (seeds/seed_name.csv)
  syntax error at or near "COLUMN"
  LINE 3:         alter table  alter column id set not null
```

If instead this worked, then this would be a useful alternative to add to https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/10551 for adding database constraints to a seed (or snapshot).

comments.author: lucidviews
comments.body:
Hi team, 

this bug seems to be back for YAML-defined snapshots. 
I'm running this in dbt Cloud on versionless and I'm getting the following server error for any macro that I call as either post- or pre-hook:
```
Compilation Error
  Could not render {{test()}}: 'test' is undefined
```

This is my snapshot definition in a Jaffle shop project:
```
snapshots:
  - name: stg_customers_snapshot
    relation: ref('stg_customers')
    config:
      database: ANALYTICS
      schema: DBT_LSILBERNAGEL
      unique_key: customer_id
      strategy: check
      check_cols: ['customer_name']
      post-hook:
        - '{{test()}}'
```

The macro is defined as:
```
{% macro test() -%}
    {{ return('SELECT 1') }}
{%- endmacro %}
```

Lmk if you need more info.

comments.author: lucidviews
comments.body:
UPDATE: 
The above behaviour is due to the underscore vs. hyphen spelling of the hook. 
Related issue: https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/10965

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body: @lucidviews Thanks for connecting this to https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/10965. That issue seems to precisely describe what you are observing for `post-hook` (hyphen) vs `post_hook` (underscore) for snapshots. The former always works in `dbt_project.yml` files, and the latter always works within properties/schema YAML files (`schema.yml`, `properties.yml`, etc.)
